newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - June 11.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - June 11.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for REUTERS by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi Tel:3324842, 3351006, 3761233 Fax:+91-11-3351006 Internet: biznis@giasbm01.vsnl.net.in
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
The Times Of India
THREE TOP OFFICIALS ARRESTED IN FODDER SCAM

Three officials belonging to the Indian Administration Service (IAS) were arrested by the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) in the animal husbandry case. The arrested are a labour commissioner, a science and technology secretary and an animal husbandry department secretary. The investigating agency has also arrested a retired IAS officer and the suspended director of the animal husbandry department. The arrests followed day-long raids at their homes by the CBI. The CBI also carried out simultaneous raids at the home of the Bihar state chief minister's private secretary.
The Economic Times
KARNATAKA OFFERS MAJOR TAX BREAKS TO IT COMPANIES

The Karnataka state government has offered exemption from payment of entry tax and purchase tax to the information technology companies planning fresh investment in the state. The concession will be on computer hardware peripherals and other capital goods including captive power sets. The IT companies will be offered a sales tax exemption for 10 years or deferment for 12 years, irrespective of the level of investment and location of the unit. This will be subject to a ceiling of 200 percent of the value of fixed assets. Such exemption deferment will also cover turnover tax without any time limit.
FLAT STEEL MAKERS PLAN TO HIKE PRICES

All domestic flat steel producers except the Steel Authority of India plan to hike their prices by 500 rupees to 1,000 rupees a tonne. The new prices are expected to take effect in the coming week for despatches in July and beyond. The rise is due to the continuous rise in the international price of steel, particularly of hot rolled coils (HRC). The Tata Iron & Steel Company is planning to hike the prices of its flat steel sproducts by about 500 rupees a tonne. Essar Steel is planning a hike of about 400 rupees a tonne for its HRC. The Lloyds Steel is planning an increase of 500 rupees to 1,000 rupees for various grades of hot rolled products.
GENERAL INSURANCE CORP FOR JOINT VENTURE IN HEALTH INSURANCE

The General Insurance Corporation of India (GIC) is talking to two U.S.-based insurance companies for a possible joint venture in the health insurance sector. The Cigna Corporation and Aetna Inc are among the two companies shortlisted by the GIC for a tie-up. Cigna International already has a representative office in India. The company also has a memorandum of understanding with the Indian pharmaceutical major Ranbaxy to set up a joint venture insurance company. GIC has, however, said it is open to tripartite agreement with each company contributing in its own area of core competency.
JAPANESE TELECOM FIRM REJECTS INDIAN ORDER

Japanese telecom giant NEC has rejected orders by the Department of Telecommunications (DoT) to supply large exchanges having 65,000 lines each against a tender for 1.3 million lines. The firm found the price offered by the DoT too high. DoT offered 5,650 rupees per line to the NEC. The lowest price quoted by Modi Alcatel against the tender was 7,298 rupees per line. But NEC has accepted orders for 68,000 lines because it wants to participate in future tenders. The NEC officials fear that if they reject the full order then DoT my blacklist the company. DoT has offered 65,000 lines to the rest of the seven manufacturers in equal quantities.
US TOPS FOREIGN INVESTMENT IN FOOD PROCESSING

The United States accounted for about 20 percent of foreign investment in the food processing sector in India in 1996/97 (April-March) with an investment of seven billion rupees. The United States was followed by Thailand and the Netherlands. Foreign investors are primarily interested in the processed food and vegetables sector, meat and poultry, milk and marine products, grain products and fermented beverages. Thailand accounts for nearly 11 percent of the foreign component in the Indian processed food industry and has invested 3.75 billion rupees. The Netherlands, the third largest investor, put up about 1.26 billion rupees (3.7 percent).
Financial Express
TELECOMMUNICATION DEPARTMENT TO BE CORPORATORISED

The communications minister said the government will soon restructure and corporatise the Department of Telecommunications (DoT). This will give DoT financial autonomy and allow it to tap the domestic and foreign debt market for funds in conformity with the debt-equity ratio allowed under the company norms. The minister, who was in Singapore to attend Asia Telecom '97, said the disinvestment of the Mahanagar Telephone Nigam (MTNL) is also on the cards. The disinvestment of MTNL and the restructuring of the DoT cannot be altogether separated, said the DoT secretary. But he did not quote a time-frame for the disinvestment.
PRESSURE MOUNTS WITHIN UF TO VETO VSNL-BT VENTURE

With the Telecom Commission indicating that a decision on the joint venture between Videsh Sanchar Nigam (VSNL) and British Telecom (BT) will be taken by the end of the month, political pressure is building within the ruling United Front to veto the proposal. Opponents say it infringes the monopoly of both VSNL and the department of telecommunications. A letter written by a Samajwadi Party MP to the telecommunications minister blasts the project. The minister, who belongs to the Samajwadi Party, is eager to push the proposal through.
EUROPEAN INVESTORS FOR SPEEDY SWITCH TO FULL CONVERTIBILITY

Major European business consortiums and leading non-resident Indian industrialists have urged the government to go in for full rupee convertibility soon. They also asked it to empower upcoming regulatory bodies to check the rising number of scandals. Welcoming the Tarapore committee report recommending full convertibility by the year 2000, the European conglomerates, which have invested heavily in India, said full convertibility of the rupee in the shortest possible time was essential for India to blend into a free market global economy.
AEROSPATIALE OPENS SHOP IN INDIA

Aerospatiale, the $10 billion French conglomerate which manufactures aircraft, helicopters, space equipment and missiles, has set up shop in India. The group is currently scouting for partnerships and joint ventures in all of its business areas. The managing director of the India liaison office of Aerospatiale said they are open to the idea of equity partnerships with Indian companies. Aerospatiale is also willing to offer just technical support to ventures here, he added. He also said they are looking at all types of partnerships as they believe in doing business through joint ventures.
RULES FOR FOREIGN NATIONALS WORKING IN INDIA RELAXED

The Reserve Bank of India has relaxed rules regarding fees payable to foreign nationals engaged by Indian companies or firms. The Home Ministry's prior clearance is no longer needed to engage foreign nationals for a period exceeding 12 months in place of the present three months. Authorised dealers (banks) have been told to permit remittances to cover the remuneration payable to foreign nationals. The only rider is that foreign nationals whose period of engagement exceeds one year should have a valid visa. If the period is up to three months, banks may accept any type of visa like tourist, business or employment visa.
Business Standard
FOREIGN TIE-UPS MAY SAVE FOREX BROKERS

Several overseas foreign exchange firms are looking to increase their presence in emerging markets, including India. The majors eyeing India include British-based firms Marshall, Exco, Harlow Butler and Tullet. The tie-up plans of overseas foreign exchange brokers are a boon to the domestic industry, which is facing a severe squeeze on profit margins. The brokerage income of leading Indian firms fell from an average of 2.5 million rupees a month in 1995/96 (April-March) to less than a million rupee a month in 1997. Since the brokerage income is falling, the revenues are not sufficient to cover the costs.
INDIA STRESSES NEED TO CURB IMPORT GROWTH

The government is working on a new uniform and transparent policy for the beverage sector. The ministries of finance, industry and food processing are at loggerheads on the Coke-Pepsi disinvestment clause. While Coke had been asked to disinvest its stake in downstream ventures, Pepsi has been allowed to continue with its 100 percent holdings which has led to a war between the two soft drink majors.
PLAN TO REGULATE RATING AGENCIES

The guidelines being framed by the Securities and Exchange Commission of India (SEBI) to regulate credit rating agencies may emphasise regulating the entry of rating agencies and recruitment of high quality personnel by these agencies. The guidelines are also expected to insist on adequate disclosures and avoidance of conflict of interest between the clients, the rating agencies and their promoters. SEBI officials met representatives of Standard & Poor's and the Securities and Exchange Commission of the United States in a bid to draw up guidelines for the rating agencies. Though both the agencies told SEBI that rating agencies are not regulated anywhere in the world, it plans to do so.
FRESH CONCESSIONS OFFERED TO BHADRAVATI POWER PROJECT

The Maharashtra state government has offered fresh concessions to the 1,082-megawatt Bhadravati power project to enable its promoters to maintain a 16.95 percent internal rate of return. The concessions were being demanded by Ispat and GEC Plc of Britain and EDF of France. The incentive of 0.6 percent for every one percent rise in plant load factor above 68.5 percent has been increased to 0.7 percent. This will result in the internal rate of return increasing by 0.57 percent.
U.S. MAY DECLARE CALLBACK SERVICES TO INDIA ILLEGAL

The Federal Communications Commission of the United States is studying a request by the Department of Telecommunications (DoT) to declare callback services to India as illegal. The DoT expects a favourable response from the U.S. regulator. Callback services take advantage of the low international telephone tariffs and reverse a call originating from a high call-tariff country to a call from a low tariff one. After the reversal, the call is treated as one from the low tariff country to the high tariff one, lowering the call charge. With its high international call tariffs, India has been a target of callback operators offering services from the United States.
The Observer
FOREIGN BANKS JOINING SPNS FACE ADDITIONAL TARIFF

Overseas banks which have decided to join the Indian Bankers Association's shared payment network system will have to pay the Department of Telecommunications (DoT) an additional tariff to maintan their respective single party network. These banks include Hong Kong Bank, Citibank, ANZ Grindlays and Standard Chartered. The tariff pertains to these banks alone as they have taken DoT's permission to remain a single party network. But they actually are part of the closed user group setup and, thereby, attract the department's closed user group tariff.
